A former accountant and naval officer, he established a network of real estate partnerships and developed major trade centres, offices and housing. His companies included Trammell Crow Company, Trammell Crow Residential and the Wyndham hotel business.

long_biography.plain_text:
Chinese jade particularly interested Dallas developer Trammell Crow, whose business travels helped introduce him and his wife, Margaret, to Asian art. Export restrictions limited purchases during their visits to China, so they acquired much of their collection through dealers, auctions and existing private collections.

The couple wanted to preserve the collection intact and make it accessible to the public. They engaged curator Clarence Shangraw to assess the works and select pieces for a permanent museum. Opened in 1998, their free museum in the Dallas Arts District presented works from China, Japan, India and other parts of Asia.
